title: 716 Gordon Street apartment approval and development charges
subtitle: Heritage designation notices, Baker Street towers and Clair Road townhouse public meetings, and plans to explore front-ending agreements.
overview: Council approved an Official Plan and zoning change for an 11-storey, 532-unit apartment building at 716 Gordon Street, near the University of Guelph {{vote:m7}}. Staff recommended approval with changes, including a wider landscape buffer along the east side. Council added a direction to invite the Mayfield Park Community Group to view and comment on the site plan {{vote:m6}}. Neighbours had raised concerns about rooftop terraces, a closer service road and the loss of mature trees.

Council received the 2023 Development Charge Results and Background Study and directed staff to investigate front-ending agreements as a growth financing tool. Staff are also to review the need for a five-year update to the by-law in the 2028-2031 budget process {{vote:m8}}. The by-law itself is expected back for approval in January 2024.

Council also gave notice of intention to designate 2187 Gordon Street under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m9}}. Statutory public meetings were held on a 136-unit stacked townhouse proposal at 331 Clair Road East {{vote:m3}} and two 15-storey towers at 55 Baker Street and 152 and 160 Wyndham Street North {{vote:m4}}. No decisions were made on either.

decisions.detail: Council approved the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments for an 11-storey, 532-unit mixed-use apartment building, following the staff-recommended modifications, with the site-plan feedback direction added {{vote:m7}}.
Council directed staff to invite the Mayfield Park Community Group to view and give feedback on the 716 Gordon Street site plan {{vote:m6}}.
Council received the 2023 Development Charge study, asked staff to investigate front-ending agreements, and asked for a review of the need for a five-year by-law update.
Council authorized notice of intention to designate 2187 Gordon Street under the Ontario Heritage Act, with the by-law returning if no objections arise in the 30-day period.
Council authorized notice of intention to designate 131 Ontario Street under the Ontario Heritage Act as part of the consent report.
Council approved demolition of the detached dwelling at 33-35 James Street West, a Part V heritage district property.

decisions.item: Baker Street and Wyndham Street North towers
decisions.detail: Council received the statutory public meeting report on a proposed rezoning for two 15-storey mixed-use towers with 353 units, with no decision yet.

debate: On 716 Gordon Street, delegates from the neighbourhood asked Council to refuse the application. They said it differed from the earlier tribunal-approved plan: the service road moved closer to homes, about 45 trees would be removed including mature evergreens, and three rooftop terraces were added. A student delegate supported it as a step toward more housing near campus.

Staff said terraces are generally permitted in zoning, and alcohol licensing is a separate process. Site plan could address barriers and noise, but staff could not require the road be moved. The decision had to be made that night because of the provincial timeline, and the developer did not agree with the staff-recommended changes.

Several councillors said they were disappointed about the trees but saw little planning basis for refusal and a low chance of success at appeal. One councillor opposed it over safety concerns about alcohol on terraces, and others said that was not a planning reason.

On development charges, a real estate association delegate said the proposed increases would add to home prices and could cancel projects. Staff said the rates are calculated under provincial rules, sit mid-range among comparator municipalities, and are kept uniform citywide so no area gets an advantage. Council discussion noted that incentives can be set up outside the by-law.

At the Clair Road East meeting, councillors questioned the reduced bike and electric vehicle parking, the play area placed beside the parking lot, and heritage conditions for moving the stone house. A phone-in delegate raised connections to neighbouring lands, privacy screening and stormwater.
